gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Distinctive from the first letter, Gugi is all tubing-thick, uniform strokes. What holds the pair together is height: both keep lowercase standing tall against their capitals, while Noto Sans Mahajani adds a funnel-wide throat in the e.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals makes Gugi stand out, its terminals cut open for a bold look. Noto Sans Mandaic keeps to the quieter work of the text, its sans-serif curves feeling unclamped.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Fine rope laid into letters: that is Gugi, distinctive and bold, with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. And Noto Sans Marchen, clean sans-serif, keeps its small letters proud, curves ending in clear daylight.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-mayan-numerals: Cut ribbon of constant width: that is Gugi. Gugi is best at making a distinctive, bold statement, while Noto Sans Mayan Numerals, a sans with tall-bodied small letters, does the steadier work.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-meetei-mayek: Noto Sans Meetei Mayek, a sans-serif, opens its rounds like a cracked bangle, with large lowercase eyes. But Gugi draws strokes that never thin or thicken, a bold uniformity that sets it apart.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-modi: Noto Sans Modi is clean and modern, with daylight inside every curve and lowercase close to capital height. And Gugi's single-weight boldness stays up in the heading while text beneath moves smoothly, line after line.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-hau: Gugi opens bold and distinctive, its tall lowercase nearly reaching the capitals, with no brush-style pressure swell anywhere. Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau reads clean, its open curves giving lines room.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-psalter-pahlavi: Distinctive and bold, Gugi draws its o as a ring with a constant wall. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi, a sans-serif with gaping e mouths and barely rising capitals, gives that boldness an approachable foil.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-runic: Bold, Gugi keeps its line width through every turn. Noto Sans Runic, in sans-serif, stands large on the line with curves that never close in, so text should flow along easily.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Bold headings, clean text: that is the arrangement. Gugi writes as if with a fixed-width nib, while Noto Sans Sundanese keeps its e crossbars open and its lowercase near capital height.
